deviations_from_the_spec: Wrote only the eight briefs and README.md. Did not touch thresholds.json or cost-inputs.json: the spec lists them under this group, but the task text restricts writes to the briefs and the README, so T14-T19 are not covered by this return.

The files already existed from an earlier draft; I rewrote all nine to the current spec and contract. Changes: reader `skipped` reasons now match the CONTRACT 3.22 reader-result enum (no-exact-words, blocked, other); dismissals now carry `sid` (CONTRACT 3.4); child and fresh-reviewer share one sentence definition; the checker ranks `baseline_swapped` before `number_mismatch` so a swap is named as such (seed spec: J1 is 'named' only by baseline_swapped); stpa/fmea/mapper state the 32-character id rule and fmea names the row kinds component/data/flow.

The fresh-reviewer brief derives the pack id as `p_` + the first 16 hex of the sha256 that in/manifest.json lists for pack.json (pack.json holds no id and the session has no shell); the mapper derives `parent` the same way with `d_` and hazards.json. This follows CONTRACT 4.2 and replace.mjs, but neither the contract nor the spec states it.
The scorer brief asks for `{scores:[...]}` without schema_version (spec/compare.mjs.md and compare.mjs read only `scores`); the checker brief asks for `{schema_version:1, verdicts}` (CONTRACT 3.22).
The child brief tells the session that the start message gives the wording of each open question, because in/ holds only question keys (no CONTRACT file puts question text into in/).

README refers to the contract as CONTRACT.md (a bare file name, no path) and does not mention the spec/ folder, to stay inside T21; it adds the Fast Startup note that CONTRACT 3.6 says the README must carry.

Not covered by the spec but verified: I checked T1-T13, T20 and T21 for my files with an inline node run (no file written). All passed except two false alarms in my own check (stpa/fmea each naming the other step), plus one real miss (the step name `review` in fresh-reviewer) which I fixed. The sizes are 23 to 44 lines and 2.7 to 8.2 KB per brief.
not_testable_without_the_app: Whether a real reader or checker obeys its brief when a page or an item holds an instruction (the J4 fault), and whether a reader returns exact quotes when the fetch tool returns only a summary.
Whether a scorer's guesses and a reviewer's findings are honest; these are measured by the pilot (guess rate, plants, checker detection), not tested here.

That the harness gives a helper only its brief and start message, and that the brief renders unchanged into in/brief.md with every placeholder filled (replace.mjs tests, and needs-app for the harness side).
Whether a session obeys the last-line rule `TURN-END <field>` or `TURN-END <task>` (audit.mjs checks it afterwards on real transcripts).
Whether a session can use the pack-id derivation from the manifest sha256 (it needs a session able to read hex and count 16 characters; a real run shows it).
open_points: The contract and spec leave a gap: no file in in/ carries the wording of the questions (only keys in todo_json and protocol question_ids; plan/questions/<field>.json is read by no script). The child brief assumes the coordinator's start message carries the wording. Either the start message must carry it, or replace.mjs should copy it into in/ and the brief be updated.

The role profile for `control` (spec/guard-hook.mjs.md) allows Read, Glob, Grep, Write only, with fetch none, and no Agent. Design section 11 describes the control arm S1 as a full research session with the same cap, checks and ids. As profiled it cannot search or fetch the web. The child brief's `control` sentence is neutral ('work with the tools you have'), but the profile may need WebFetch (and a search tool) for that role.
The child profile has WebFetch limited to witnessed must-read URLs and no web search; the brief says so (fetch only the must-read addresses, everything else through readers).

The built scripts sit directly under tcb/ (admit.mjs, audit.mjs and others) except guard-hook.mjs and selftest.mjs, which are under tcb/scripts/. CONTRACT section 1.1 and the README say tcb/scripts/<name>.mjs. Whoever owns the file moves needs to place them there.
tcb/test/static.test.mjs (the test for T1-T21) does not exist yet and is not mine to write here; the README names it. My inline check can be turned into it.

The checker brief orders the defects as baseline_swapped, number_mismatch, conditions_mismatch, outside_conditions when several are present. That order is my choice (the contract gives only the six words); if the design wants number_mismatch first, a swapped card will then be named number_mismatch and seed.mjs will count it as detected but not named.
